system_description.narrative_title: Escalating US–Iran conflict and Middle East energy shock
system_description.narrative_summary: A spiraling security confrontation—between the United States, Iran, and Iran-aligned proxies (notably the Houthis)—is driving military posturing, evacuations, diplomatic shuttle diplomacy and market panic, producing sharp spikes in oil, freight and insurance costs. Treated as an open system, cross-border flows (energy exports, shipping, information, military action, and financial sentiment) transmit shocks and feedbacks: attacks and threats fuel price and supply disruptions, which in turn shape political choices, allied responses and further security actions. External inputs (U.S. domestic politics, Saudi/OPEC policy, global demand) and adaptive actors (navies, insurers, traders, diplomats) continuously modulate the system’s trajectory.
system_description.scope: Regional security–energy–trade system centered on US–Iran hostilities and proxy attacks: military operations and posturing, Houthi strikes on shipping and Saudi assets, Gulf oil production and tanker routes, evacuations and embassy/security measures, and resulting effects on global oil/freight markets and corporate costs.
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical-economic system (global energy markets, international trade, strategic alliances and financial markets).
adjacent_subsystems: Global crude oil markets and trading infrastructure
Maritime shipping, insurance and freight logistics
Gulf states' security architecture and internal stability
U.S. domestic politics and electoral/tactical timelines

variables.name: Conflict escalation pressure
variables.description: The aggregate propensity for kinetic escalation in the region, measured by the frequency, intensity and tempo of armed actions and explicit threats.

variables.name: Proxy attack activity
variables.description: The rate and intensity of operations carried out by aligned non-state groups or proxy forces across land, sea and air domains.

variables.name: Naval military posture
variables.description: The concentration, readiness and maneuvering of maritime military assets that affect sea-control and escort/ interdiction capabilities.

variables.name: Maritime attack rate
variables.description: The frequency and severity of hostile actions directed at commercial shipping, tankers and port infrastructure.

variables.name: Shipping route accessibility
variables.description: The degree to which key sea lanes and chokepoints are open to safe, timely commercial transit, including closures and detours.

variables.name: Oil export volume
variables.description: The physical volumetric flow of crude oil and refined petroleum products leaving the region for international markets.

variables.name: Crude oil price level
variables.description: The prevailing market price level for benchmark crude grades reflecting supply–demand balance and risk premia.

variables.name: Freight and tanker rate level
variables.description: The prevailing cost level for chartering and shipping cargo and tankers on major maritime routes.

variables.name: Insurance premium level
variables.description: The average risk premium charged by insurers for war, piracy and political-risk cover on maritime and energy shipments.

variables.name: Strategic oil reserves
variables.description: The aggregate volume of stored crude and product inventories held as buffers against supply disruptions.

variables.name: Market volatility expectation
variables.description: The collective expectation of future price volatility among traders and financial markets for energy and regional assets.

variables.name: Investor risk aversion
variables.description: The average willingness of investors to hold regionally exposed equities, bonds and commodities given geopolitical risk.

variables.name: Diplomatic de‑escalation effort
variables.description: The intensity and frequency of formal and informal diplomatic initiatives aimed at reducing tensions and negotiating accommodations.

variables.name: Trade route reliability
variables.description: The continuity and predictability of overland and maritime trade corridors in delivering goods without delay or interdiction.

variables.name: Undersea infrastructure risk
variables.description: The vulnerability and operational risk facing submarine cables, pipelines and buried communications that sustain trade and finance.

variables.name: Global oil demand level
variables.description: The aggregate worldwide consumption demand for crude oil and petroleum products that sets the baseline pressure on markets.

catalysts.title: US midterm elections (2026-11-04)
catalysts.description: US national elections that can shift US foreign-policy incentives and timing for military or diplomatic moves relating to Iran.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines warn markets are 'on edge ahead of the weekend, as midterm elections near' and embassies tighten security.

catalysts.title: Qatari-mediated diplomatic talks in Tehran
catalysts.description: Qatari mediators are in Tehran in a U.S.-coordinated effort to ease tensions — a near-term diplomatic push that can reduce escalation pressure.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Qatari mediators in Tehran for U.S.-coordinated effort to ease tensions.'

catalysts.title: Renewed Houthi attacks on Saudi and shipping
catalysts.description: Continued Houthi strikes against Saudi targets and maritime actors, likely to persist and disrupt regional trade and energy infrastructure.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Houthis say they targeted Saudi oil sites; attacks reported in Aden' and continued Houthi attacks cited.

catalysts.title: Potential new US military strikes against Iran
catalysts.description: Statements and intelligence assessments increase the near-term possibility of additional US kinetic operations against Iranian targets.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Trump says US may do another military operation against Iran' and strikes are predicted ahead of midterms.

catalysts.title: US carrier rearming/repositioning (USS George Washington)
catalysts.description: Rearming and forward posture of a US carrier group prepared for possible strikes, raising near-term military readiness in the Gulf.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Aboard USS George Washington as It Rearms for Possible Iran Strikes.'

catalysts.title: Iranian threats to undersea cables and infrastructure
catalysts.description: Iran has articulated plans to target Gulf undersea cables if conflict resumes, raising the risk to submarine infrastructure and connectivity.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Iran has detailed plans to hit Gulf undersea cables if war resumes, officials say.'

catalysts.title: Saudi Aramco stockpile expansion efforts
catalysts.description: Saudi Aramco seeking partners to expand oil stockpiles, which would boost strategic reserves and influence regional export flows and prices.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Saudi Aramco seeks to partner with countries to expand its oil stockpile, CEO says.'

catalysts.title: US evacuations and outpost withdrawals
catalysts.description: US withdrawals/evacuations of personnel from regional outposts and tightened embassy security that alter force posture and risk signalling.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'U.S. Evacuates Mideast Outposts...' and 'US orders some personnel to leave Saudi Arabia.'

catalysts.title: Soaring tanker rates and insurance premiums
catalysts.description: Rapidly rising tanker charter costs and war-risk insurance driven by regional insecurity that amplify shipping costs and energy squeeze.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'soaring tanker rates trigger a second energy squeeze' and oil prices approach Iran-war highs.
